newsitem.title: FRANCE: OECD sees upward pressure on Dutch wages, prices.
newsitem.headline: OECD sees upward pressure on Dutch wages, prices.

text.p: The OECD said on Thursday that the Dutch economy would continue to grow at a robust pace in 1997 and 1998 but that this would also bring inflationary pressures.
The OECD forecast in its June economic outlook that real Dutch GDP growth would pick up slightly to 3.2 percent in 1998 from 3.0 percent in 1997.
"With output rising above potential, and due to the recent depreciation of the guilder in effective terms, some upward pressure on wages and prices is likely to emerge," it said.
The OECD said that in the past the Netherlands had usually closely followed economic developments in Germany.
More recently, however, there had been a pronounced decoupling, with the Netherlands performing "significantly better" than Germany and other neighbouring countries.
"The Dutch economy is apparently benefiting from several years of wage moderation combined with structural reforms in the labour market and the social security system..." it said.
Consumer spending was likely to slow down in 1997 and 1998 after showing strong growth in 1996.

However, an effective depreciation of the guilder and a likely economic upturn in Europe should boost exports which were set to take over as the driving force behind overall economic growth, the OECD said.
"With output rising above potential and with a somewhat lower effective exchange rate, some inflationary pressures are likely to emerge," it said.
There were some uncertainties as to how wages and prices would react to this "incipient overheating", it added.
The outcome, it said, would depend in part on the strength of the expected upturn in Europe and exchange rate developments.
